problems.stem: The Module 1 readiness checklist asks you to confirm "my resume bullets show measurable results." How should you check this box honestly?
options: Check it because you finished the resume section.
Open your resume, confirm each bullet has an action verb plus a number or outcome, and only then check the box.
Check every box at once to save time.
Leave it unchecked since checklists do not matter.
problems.explanation: A readiness check is a real test, not a formality. Verify the artifact meets the standard before marking it complete.

problems.stem: You are finalizing one shared profile slide for the studio. Which approach reflects that the module's skills work together?
options: Make it look polished and ignore the other module skills.
Check that it has truthful evidence, a disclosed AI-use note, alt text on its image, and no exposed private data, all at once.
Apply only the resume skill, since that is the main one.
Run a single AI pass and assume it handled everything.
problems.explanation: The module's skills combine in one artifact. Readiness means evidence, AI disclosure, accessibility, and privacy are all handled together.

problems.stem: You ask the studio's AI, "Am I ready for Module 2?" and it replies "Yes, you are ready." How should you treat this?
options: Accept it and move on; the studio decided.
Use it as a prompt to inspect your own artifacts against each target, since you confirm readiness, not the tool.
Ask three more times until you get a different answer.
Skip checking your artifacts because the AI is confident.
problems.explanation: The studio supports your self-assessment but does not replace it. You verify readiness by checking your own evidence against the standards.

problems.stem: Going through the checklist, you find your privacy skill is still shaky: you have not enabled two-factor authentication. What is the most useful thing to record?
options: Mark privacy as complete so the module looks finished.
Flag privacy as a gap and request targeted practice on enabling two-factor authentication.
Hide the gap and hope it does not come up later.
Delete the privacy item from the checklist.
problems.explanation: An honestly flagged gap routes you to the right practice. A false all-clear hides exactly the skill you most need to build.

problems.stem: Your readiness checklist flagged 'no two-factor authentication' as a gap. You just walked through your account's 2FA setup screens. Can you mark the privacy row 'pass'?
options: Yes; you performed the fix, so the gap is closed.
Not yet: re-open the account's security settings and confirm 2FA is actually showing as enabled before the row earns its pass.
Yes, as long as you note the date you made the change.
No; privacy rows can never be marked pass.
problems.explanation: The distinctive failure of checklist work is fixing a gap and forgetting to re-inspect it. Setup flows fail silently (an unconfirmed code, an unsaved toggle), so the loop closes only when the artifact itself shows the fixed state. Inspect, fix, re-inspect.
